title: The dispatch viewer treats only d001 as a readback, so a resumed create's later readback reads as orchestrator work
foundBy: user report (host), after SAC-055's fix showed that a resumed create can put a member's readback past d001: "fix the dispatch viewer (frames.go) so it no longer assumes the readback is always d001 when a create was resumed"
details:
**What happens.** `cs-dispatch-viewer` decides which dispatches are create-time readbacks partly by the literal id `d001`. A resumed create, or a readback asked for a second time, puts a member's readback at `d002` or later. That breaks two findings.

- `accept-of-readback` fires only for `d001`. A log that accepts `dev/d002`, where `d002` is dev's readback, reports nothing.
- `reply-not-accepted` falls back to `d001` alone when the archive's message times are clobbered. dev's `d002` readback is then reported as orchestrator work nobody accepted. It is a warning when later work followed and severe when it is the node's last dispatch, as in a failed create.

**How to reproduce.** Build an archive in which dev's `d001` readback failed, a resumed create asked again in `d002`, and the mission then sent `d003`. Load it with `frames.Load`. With real message times, an accept of `dev/d002` yields no finding. With clobbered times, `dev/d002` yields `reply-not-accepted`.

**Why it matters.** The viewer is how a run is audited afterwards. A readback shown as unjudged work sends a reader looking for a failure that did not happen. An acceptance of a readback shown as normal hides an orchestrator judging what the host judges.

**Where it is.** The two checks are `buildEventsAndSpans` and `check`, in `dispatch-viewer/internal/frames/frames.go`. The finding's definition in `issueDefs` and MANUAL.md also names `d001`.
